clue.text: Taylor Swift not one we disturbed in dysfunctional hotel

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are thrown out of order and reset
not one says the singer's name loses its single I

parts.note: the singer's name is used letter for letter as raw material
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pop star's visit causes chaos at a hotel that is already badly run.
explanation.walkthrough: FAWLTY TOWERS was a 1970s BBC sitcom set in a chaotic Torquay hotel run by Basil Fawlty.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional hotel in the sitcom is famously mismanaged, so a dysfunctional establishment describes it well.

clue.text: Pair in trouble for month

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A couple in difficulties for a whole calendar month.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth division of the calendar year is one of the twelve named months.

clue.text: Take furtive look round cool street in Midlands city

indicators.note: the leering look goes round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to leer is to cast a sly, furtive glance
ice cools, and to ice something is to chill it

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks a glance around a chilly street in an English Midlands city.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a large city in the East Midlands region of England.

clue.text: Royal house about to return delivery

parts.note: the House of York was an English royal dynasty

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A royal dynasty about to come back into power.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a yorker is a ball pitched right at the batter's feet, hard to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bowler's ball is called a delivery, and this is one particular type of ball.

clue.text: SOS involving British Conservative in tearful tale

indicators.note: involving means taking the other pieces into the middle

parts.note: taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A distress call from a British politician turns into a weepy story.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a sad account told to win sympathy, a tale designed to bring tears.

clue.text: Any idiot with costume cast for 1 Across 12 Across perhaps

indicators.note: cast in the sense of moulding afresh, reshaping the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Fawlty Towers is a classic example of the television sitcom genre.

clue.text: Singer in Italian port to north-east

parts.note: Bari is a port on Italy's Adriatic coast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vocalist is found in a southern Italian harbour city, off to the north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male vocalist with a voice between tenor and bass.

clue.text: Deliberately lose most of the argument

indicators.note: most of a word means all of it except its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a debate on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a game or contest is to lose it on purpose, often for a bribe.

clue.text: Ring road repaired by East River

indicators.note: repaired roadwork is rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Road works on a ring road near an eastern river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is the river forming part of the border between the US and Mexico.

clue.text: Trio at bar disorderly — right for one to settle dispute?

indicators.note: disorderly signals that the letters are jumbled out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Three rowdy drinkers at a pub need someone to sort out their quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbitrator is an impartial person appointed to judge and resolve a disagreement.

clue.text: Aussie bouncer initially tempting batsman Joe

parts.note: a kangaroo, or roo, bounds along, so it is an Australian bouncer

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: An Australian fast bowler's bouncer tempts an England batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a short-pitched cricket ball; the bouncer is a kangaroo. Joe Root is an England Test cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Root is a celebrated English cricketer, so batsman Joe identifies him by his surname.

clue.text: Might this soothe a depressed-sounding woman?

parts.note: a low means a depressed, as in feeling a bit down
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Wondering what might cheer up a woman feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: The gel of this succulent plant is used as a soothing balm for burns and irritated skin.

clue.text: Harmless boozer with old US coin

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub
a cent is a US coin worth one hundredth of a dollar

explanation.surface: A pub drinker carrying an old American penny seems quite harmless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something innocent is inoffensive and causes no injury.

clue.text: One doing the Lord's work?

parts.note: the surface suggests a priest or missionary serving God
the setter means the trade Jesus learned from Joseph in Nazareth

explanation.walkthrough: Jesus is traditionally said to have worked as a woodworker before his ministry, so his literal job is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus is held to have followed the woodworking trade, so anyone in that trade does his earthly job.

parts.note: bigots are prejudiced, intolerant people

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A congressman's dazzling scandal involves a thousand dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the US House of Representatives; the astrological house is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrological house is associated with a zodiac sign, which stands for it.

clue.text: Channel having no bends we hear

parts.note: something straight has no curves

explanation.surface: A channel with no curves in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow sea passage linking two larger bodies of water.

clue.text: Make every effort in Lorna's flat? Most desirable!

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel, so Lorna's means Doone's
flat means level
best means most desirable

explanation.surface: An estate agent's pitch for a novel heroine's apartment: the finest!
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's 1869 novel set on Exmoor; the surface's 'flat' is an apartment, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's level best is an idiom for trying as hard as one can.

clue.text: Material used in many longbows

clue.text: Honestly, deviously or surreptitiously?

explanation.surface: Asking whether something was done truthfully or by sneaky means.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposites honestly and deviously mislead; one word's letters supply the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: On the sly is an idiom meaning secretly or furtively.

clue.text: See 21
Genuine old Spanish coin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether a Spanish coin is authentic; the two senses are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means authentic and also names a former silver coin of Spain.

clue.text: Ruinous to Eve with vicar doing too much?

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Is ready and gives support

definitions.meaning: first meaning: is waiting prepared to act
second meaning: backs or stays loyal to someone

explanation.definitionFit: The verb phrase covers both waiting in readiness and remaining loyal to a person.

clue.text: Time to race along — hard going for creature
